name: Deep magenta
lede: Deep magenta is a dark, saturated magenta, built from the modifier "deep" in front of the base color rather than from any separate tradition of its own.

sections.title: A modifier, not a separate name
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[hyacinth-violet]], [[dark-magenta]], [[iris-purple]] and [[purple-munsell]], at 3.7, 4.3, 5.8 and 5.8 ΔE [1]. It comes from the 2010 xkcd color survey, where a visitor's typed label for this darker, lower-lightness cluster of the magenta family won out over other wording [1].

Because it is a modifier rather than a standalone dictionary word, Deep magenta is not in our library of CSS, Ridgway, Maerz and Paul, or ISCC-NBS names; only its parent [[magenta]] carries that older pedigree [1]. At lightness 38 and chroma 78, it sits noticeably darker than typical magenta while keeping nearly the same hue angle [1]. Nearby in the same family are [[purple]], [[magenta]], and [[plum]], all sharing the same reddish-purple corner of the wheel [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this dark magenta covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. Dyes and pigments able to hold magenta's hue at this depth and saturation are a modern, largely synthetic achievement, so the gap is expected rather than a gap in the data [2].
